messages.content: What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?

message.content:
The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is the most recent common ancestor of the two families **Felidae** (cats) and **Equidae** (horses).  
In terms of higher taxonomy this ancestor lies at the node that separates the order **Carnivora** (which contains Felidae) from the order **Perissodactyla** (which contains Equidae).  
That node represents the last common ancestor of all modern carnivorans and perissodactyls, and it dates back to the early Eocene, roughly 50–55 million years ago.
